clue.text: Be grateful for rise in value

definitions.meaning: to value or be thankful for a kindness
what an asset does when it gains worth over time

explanation.surface: Someone thanks another for a gift that has gained worth.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both thankfulness for something and an investment's growth in worth, two senses of the same word.

clue.text: Meet and stay with royal characters

parts.note: a stay is a support or prop
ER, Elizabeth Regina, are the royal letters on a postbox or coin

explanation.surface: An invitation to greet and lodge with members of the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meet' is the old adjective meaning fitting or suitable, not the verb it looks like.
explanation.definitionFit: Meet as an adjective means suitable or appropriate, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Think to show spirit in a note

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane
taken as written
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A drinker is told to reflect by displaying a bottle of liquor beside a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: To think something over at length is to ponder or mull it.

clue.text: Police records under "Swindles"

indicators.note: in a down clue the records piece is written beneath the swindles piece

parts.note: cons are swindles or tricks
tables are records or lists of data

explanation.surface: Police files are kept beneath a heading about frauds.
explanation.definitionFit: Constables are officers of the police force, so the plural stands for the police.

clue.text: Nauseated by the music?

parts.note: music is an air, so someone sickened by a tune is jokingly sick of the air, though the real word means queasy on a flight

explanation.definitionFit: The real sense is feeling sick from the motion of flying, here punningly tied to a tune, an air.

clue.text: It's always right to support the first mate

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath the one it holds up

parts.note: Eve was Adam's mate, the first wife in Genesis

explanation.surface: A claim that a husband is always right to back his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means at all times, a synonym of always.

clue.text: Left some legal document lying around

indicators.note: the deed is described as lying around the other piece, so it encloses it

parts.note: a deed is a signed legal document
part means some of something

explanation.surface: Someone went away leaving part of a legal paper lying about.
explanation.definitionFit: Departed means gone away, the same as having left.

clue.text: Fresh answer found, so permission is given to proceed

parts.note: green means fresh or new
a light is an answer entered in a crossword grid

explanation.surface: A new solution is found, so a project is cleared to go ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: LIGHT for a crossword answer is a solver's convention; the definition paraphrases the phrase as the authorisation to go ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from traffic signals, where the go-ahead colour means you may proceed.

clue.text: Having half-done lining, turn facing

indicators.note: the half word sits inside the turn word like a lining inside a coat

parts.note: to veer is to turn or swerve

indicators.note: only the second half of the word done is kept

explanation.surface: A tailor's note: with the lining half finished, turn the facing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps NE, the back half of DONE, which lines VEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A veneer is a thin surface layer of fine wood, a facing over cheaper material.

clue.text: A scholar without scholarship at Westminster?

definitions.text: A scholar without scholarship at Westminster?

parts.words: A scholar without scholarship at Westminster?
parts.note: at Westminster School a pupil not holding a scholarship is called by a word that also means one of the ordinary people, not the Lords, who sit at Westminster

explanation.walkthrough: Westminster School is an old London public school; Westminster is also Parliament, where the lower house holds the non-noble members.
explanation.definitionFit: At some English schools and colleges a fee-paying pupil without a scholarship has this title, which also means an ordinary citizen.

clue.text: Sing, quite unperturbed about puff needed

indicators.note: the calm word goes about, or around, the advert

parts.note: serene means completely calm and untroubled
a puff is a piece of promotion, an advertisement or ad

explanation.surface: A singer is told to stay calm even though breath is required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puff' looks like breath for singing but is a short advertisement, AD.
explanation.definitionFit: To serenade someone is to sing to them, typically beneath a window.

clue.text: A touching article or tract

parts.note: re means concerning or touching on
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A moving essay or pamphlet is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tract' poses as a pamphlet but means a stretch of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is an expanse or region of land, an area.

clue.text: Teetotal seaman making his mark?…

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
staining something leaves a mark on it

explanation.surface: A sailor who doesn't drink leaves his signature.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone teetotal is refraining from alcohol altogether.

clue.text: Chance for a love-lorn Westerner

indicators.note: lorn means bereft, so the Westerner word loses the letter for love

parts.note: an occidental is a person from the West
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: An opportunity arises for a lonely Western man pining for love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love-lorn' looks like one word for pining, but splits: 'love' is the letter to drop and 'lorn' (bereft of) is the deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chance used as an adjective means happening by luck, not by design.

clue.text: … and the dramatist encouraging him?

definitions.meaning: John ... was an English playwright, author of Abraham Lincoln
the teetotal seaman of the previous clue would be urged to take only plain liquid instead of alcohol

explanation.surface: A playwright cheers on the sober sailor of the previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 12-down: the teetotaller is told to drink water.
explanation.definitionFit: The playwright's surname is the same as the advice to take plain liquid instead of alcohol.

clue.text: Insidious about a national emblem in a smooth sort of way

definitions.text: in a smooth sort of way

indicators.note: the sly word goes about, or around, the emblem

parts.note: sly means cunning and insidious
the leek is the national emblem of Wales

explanation.surface: A sneaky manner around a country's symbol is described as smooth.
explanation.walkthrough: The LEEK is a vegetable worn as the emblem of Wales on St David's Day.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in a glossy, polished manner, as of sleek fur or manners.

clue.text: From page one, a good book for an interpreter

parts.note: ex means from, as in ex works
taken as written
NT is the New Testament, part of the Good Book

explanation.surface: A translator works from the first page of a fine volume.
explanation.definitionFit: An exponent is one who expounds or performs a work, an interpreter of it.

clue.text: After getting discharged go back for support of a kind

indicators.note: the turned piece comes after the discharged piece

parts.note: fired means discharged, as from a job or a gun

indicators.note: back says the word go is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Someone sacked goes back looking for help.
explanation.walkthrough: A firedog is a metal log stand in a hearth; 'support of a kind' hides this behind the sense of help for the sacked worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A firedog is an andiron, a metal stand supporting logs in a fireplace.

clue.text: Trumpeter disturbs the panel

indicators.note: disturbing the letters of the words throws them into a new order

explanation.surface: A trumpet player upsets the judging panel.
explanation.definitionFit: An elephant trumpets through its trunk, so it is a trumpeter in crossword terms.

clue.text: "How hard it is for women to keep —!" (J Caesar)

definitions.text: "How hard it is for women to keep —!" (J Caesar)

parts.words: "How hard it is for women to keep —!" (J Caesar)
parts.note: Portia's line in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar; the missing word means a secret or private advice

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase to keep counsel means to keep a secret, as Portia laments in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Staff seeing plane crash in front of store

indicators.note: the anagram is placed in front of the store word
a crash wrecks the word plane, rearranging its letters

parts.note: stock is a store or supply

explanation.surface: An observer sees an aircraft come down outside a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpenstock is a long iron-tipped staff used by mountain walkers.

clue.text: Land in the river

parts.note: describes a small island in a river, especially the Thames, rather than ground beside it

explanation.definitionFit: The word, also spelt ait, is a small island in a river.

clue.text: Love to strive for superiority over the party in Spain

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pieces sit above the party piece

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
to vie is to compete for the upper hand
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Romance competes with politics for dominance at a Spanish party.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is a city in Spain, in northern Asturias.
explanation.definitionFit: Oviedo is the capital city of Asturias, located in northern Spain.

clue.text: The number of, say, the whole of the Bar

definitions.text: The number of, say, the whole of the Bar

parts.words: The number of, say, the whole of the Bar
parts.note: say signals that whole sounds like hole; the clubhouse bar is jokingly the golf course's extra hole after the eighteenth

explanation.walkthrough: 'the Bar' suggests barristers; it is the golf club bar, the 19th hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers call the clubhouse bar the nineteenth hole, the one after the round's eighteen.

clue.text: A little like a strong point

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something a bit like a stronghold or fortified position.
explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the four cardinal points of the compass.

clue.text: More than satisfied with state-aid as distributed

indicators.note: distributing the letters spreads them into a new order

explanation.surface: Recipients are overfed with government subsidy handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Satiated means filled to excess, beyond merely satisfied.

clue.text: Prior occupying quarters in a French town

indicators.note: the prior word takes up position inside the quarters

parts.note: N and S, north and south, are quarters of the compass
ante is Latin for before, prior

explanation.surface: An earlier tenant living in rooms in a French town.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantes is a city on the Loire in western France.

clue.text: No-one thanks soldiers very much for returning allowance

indicators.note: returning says the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: no plus one, written as the Roman numeral I
ta is British slang for thanks
RE is the Royal Engineers
a lot means very much

explanation.surface: Nobody thanks the troops heartily for coming home on leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns NOITARELOT round; 'No-one' gives NO and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Toleration is the act of allowing or permitting something, an allowance of it.
